# D&D Dashboard

> A live Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition character sheet for the whole table.
> Players keep their character here instead of on paper; the Dungeon Master sees
> the party's vital stats update in real time and runs combat from the same data.

The app is a single-page dashboard at https://dnd.jgulfo.com. It is free, has no
ads, and requires a Google sign-in because every character is stored privately
per account. English and Spanish are both supported, at /en and /es; the root URL
detects the browser's preferred language and forwards to one of them.

It is an unofficial, non-commercial fan project by Jesus Gulfo
(https://jgulfo.com). It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Wizards of the
Coast, and it does not reproduce the rules text of any D&D book. It tracks the
numbers for a character you have already made.

## What a player gets

A full 5e character sheet where the derived numbers are computed, not typed:

- Header: name, race, class, subclass, background, alignment and level, plus AC,
  speed, initiative, proficiency bonus, hit dice and passive perception.
- Ability scores: the six abilities, with modifiers, saving throw bonuses, spell
  save DC, spell attack bonus and passive perception all derived from the base
  scores.
- Skills: the eighteen 5e skills, each set to not proficient, proficient or
  expertise, with bonuses derived from the governing ability.
- Health: current, maximum and temporary HP, a bar that marks the character as
  bloodied at half HP, and death saving throws. Temporary HP is signed, so a
  negative value represents a maximum-HP debuff.
- Combat: an attack list with hit bonus, damage, type (melee, ranged or special)
  and notes.
- Spellcasting: spell slots by level and a prepared-spell list with cast time,
  range, duration, concentration and ritual flags.
- Equipment and inventory: gear slots with modifiers, a pack with quantities and
  icons, and a coin purse.
- Resources: custom class resource trackers (ki points, sorcery points, Channel
  Divinity and so on), each tagged as short rest or long rest so the rest
  buttons reset the right ones.
- Traits and notes: freeform cards for features, quests, NPCs and rumors. Notes
  can be shared with the party or kept private, and can be dictated by voice.
- Rests: a short rest resets only short-rest resources; a long rest restores HP,
  every spell slot, death saves and all resources.

## What a Dungeon Master gets

Choosing the DM role on first sign-in swaps the character sheet for a party
dashboard:

- A live party grid. Players enable sharing and hand over their ID; from then on
  the DM sees each character's HP, temporary HP, conditions, passive perception,
  spell save DC and remaining spell slots update as they change.
- A combat and initiative tracker. The DM adds monsters (with HP, AC, initiative
  and a quantity that spawns identical copies) and offline players who are at the
  table without the app, then drives the turn order. Monster names and stats stay
  hidden as "????" until the DM reveals them.
- Damage attribution. Damage is credited to whoever dealt it, producing a
  per-combat leaderboard and a victory or defeat summary when combat ends.
- When the DM starts combat, every player's screen opens a full-screen combat
  view with their HP hero card, conditions and the live turn order.

## Technical shape

Next.js 16 App Router, React 19 and Tailwind CSS v4, built as a static export and
served from Cloudflare Pages. Auth and persistence are Firebase (Google sign-in
plus Firestore), so the page renders its content in the browser after sign-in:
what a crawler or an unauthenticated fetch receives is the shell and this
metadata, not a character sheet.
